action_summary: Deletes the world model from planning and measures what is left. On a real clone of pypa/packaging, 6 real damaged states and 10 real git actions, the planner copies the state, runs the action and reads the exit status: one execution yields both applicability and the exact successor, so the search runs over real directories and predicts nothing (transitions_predicted = 0). Learned-conditions pruning solves 6 of 7 in 658 executions (318 edges deleted); the no-knowledge control solves 7 of 7 in 1315; using the same knowledge only to ORDER solves 7 of 7 in 1337. Pruning buys 50% and loses one task in seven -- the only soundness cost in the whole design, and the conditions are never named (0 of 10 identified) while still deleting edges. Three goals were falsified by plans: a cleanliness goal is satisfied by dropping the stash (destroys the work), an identity goal makes the rescue unsatisfiable (204 executions, 0 solved), and the content goal was satisfied by committing the mess onto the branch it was on (found by the search, not by review) until every other branch tip was pinned. The remaining designed part is the dedup KEY: a coarse key silently made the search incomplete (0 of 3 hard tasks at 1500 expansions); keying on staged/dirty/untracked/stash counts and the operation in progress solved them at depth 5, 6, 6. 0 parameters, 0 model calls, 0 transitions predicted.

next_step: Keep the branch and the exact successor; treat learned conditions as an ORDERING with a budget, never as a deletion (ordering cannot lose a task, deletion already did); and spend the effort on goals that name the content that must survive, verified adversarially by the search.
real_outcome: That a real repair of a real repository needs no world model at all: one copy plus one execution returns the applicability decision AND the exact successor, so the planner searches over real states, and 5 of 6 damaged states were repaired in the learned stream and 6 of 6 in the control, each verified by git itself. That the only unsound component is the learned condition used to DELETE work (50% fewer executions, one task in seven lost, conditions named 0 of 10), while the same knowledge used to ORDER bought nothing (1337 vs 1315). That the remaining designed part is the dedup key, not the model, and that the binding constraint on the whole idea is the specification: three successive goals were satisfied by plans that destroyed a stash, a history, or another branch.

truth.the_law_this_round_adds: EXACTNESS IS FREE, COMPLETENESS IS NOT. Copying a state and running the action makes the successor exact at the price of one execution and deletes the world model entirely (0 transitions predicted). What remains expensive is branching, and what remains unsound is any prior strong enough to cut it: the conditions that deleted 318 edges were named 0 of 10 times and lost one task in seven. A prior that only orders is safe and worth 0 here. So the parts left are a key that separates the states the goal can tell apart, and a goal that cannot be satisfied by throwing away what the owner cares about.
